analysis:
Integration pass over the GPT-OSS stop-scope change. Production changes replayed: ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope delegates to ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope, which returns GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope (opener '<|channel|>final', openerEnd '<|message|>', closers end/return/call/start). EngineV2SlotFactory.swift:574 passes the scope through EngineV2Factory.makeBridge into an immutable EngineV2Bridge.stopStringScope, then EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249-250 and EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request forward it to CBv2Request. The value is derived from the catalog modelId and config modelType, not from consumer input, and it is not folded into cacheSalt or the checkpoint scope. T-041 mitigations (coordinator-authored cacheSalt, HMAC tags, 30-minute TTL, SSD paths) are untouched. Encryption (T-008), attestation, authorization and TB-011/TB-012 are untouched.

EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift adds a scope-aware replay through StopHoldback.ingest that only reports which stop candidate ended generation. The unscoped path is unchanged. Residual risk is a diagnostic or reporting mismatch, not confidentiality. A consumer stop string that never matches in the final channel could let generation run to max_tokens, which is bounded by max_tokens and cancellation (T-010).

A new MLXServerGenerationEvent `.logprobs` case is handled as pass-through in GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift:101 and ignored in JSONAnswerFormat.swift:81. InferenceErrorClassifier.swift:42 classifies .responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens as a non-provider-fault retryable reason, and ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift:249 maps it to 422. Production emission of logprobs is in the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule, whose pointer moved from aee6ebb to 2beb401 with no diff supplied; libs/mlx and libs/mlx-swift also moved. Those submodule contents, including CBv2StopStringScope and StopHoldback, are unreviewed. The provider-side logprobs and held-back text paths (GLM5Next pass-through, JSON-answer withholding) should be checked against the submodule to confirm that logprobs cannot leak withheld stop-sequence, reasoning or invalid-JSON content. The test changes and docs/changelog are benign. No concrete regression is supported by the supplied evidence, but the submodule bumps remain an unverified contract, so I flag deeper review.
